| Feature derivation | Created `edu_group` (Below bachelor's / Bachelor's / Advanced degree) from `ba`, `adv`. | `educ99` is missing for whole survey years; `ba`/`adv` are complete, so every row keeps an education control. | 1 new column |
| Consistency | Removed 0 rows with age < 16 or impossible weeks/hours. | Values outside the valid CPS ranges are data errors. | 0 rows |
| Consistency | Clipped 0 negative `potexp` values to 0 and recomputed `potexp2`. | Potential experience = age - schooling - 6 becomes negative when schooling is long relative to age; negative experience is meaningless, and `potexp2` must stay consistent with `potexp`. | 0 rows |
| Target | Removed 0 rows with `realhrwage` missing or <= 0. | log(wage) is undefined; zero hourly wages are unpaid/zero-hours artefacts rather than real wage offers. | 0 rows |
| Outliers (top-coding) | Detected yearly top-codes of `incwage` and added flag `top_coded` (671 rows); rows kept. | Top-coding is censoring, not an error. Men are more often at the cap, so dropping these rows would understate the gender gap. | 671 rows flagged |
| Outliers (extreme wages) | Winsorized ln(realhrwage) at the 1%/99% percentiles ($4.03–$87.70/h); 6,872 values clipped, none deleted. | Hourly wages derived from tiny hours/near-zero income are implausible; clipping limits their leverage on regression coefficients while keeping every worker in the sample. Raw version retained as `ln_realhrwage_raw`. | 6,872 values |
| Transformation | Target = `ln_realhrwage` (natural log of real hourly wage, winsorized); also added `ln_incwage`. | Skewness drops from 572.48 to 0.08; coefficients on the log scale are approximate % wage differences (Mincer equation), the standard in wage-gap research. | 2 new columns |
| Aggregation / sampling | No row sampling for modelling; saved weighted year × sex summary to `docs/results/agg_year_sex.csv`. | Full data fits in memory (subsampling would only reduce precision). The aggregate supports the time-trend question (RQ1) and keeps the survey weights. | 14 aggregate rows |
| Feature selection | Excluded 99 raw helper / income columns (o_*, q* flags, other income variables) from the features. | o_* hold unedited original values, q* are imputation flags; other income columns (e.g. inclongj, srcearn) are target leakage. | 99 columns |
| Feature selection | Excluded `un_lnrealwg` (uncensored log wage = target leakage) and 25 nominal code / id columns. | un_lnrealwg is the target itself; the code columns are nominal labels (occupation, industry, birthplace, ...) that would be wrongly treated as numbers; occupation and industry are already represented by dummies and adj_occ2name. | 28 columns |
| Encoding | Did not one-hot `edu_group` (kept `ba`, `adv` dummies instead). | `edu_group` is an exact function of `ba`/`adv`; its dummies would be perfectly collinear with them. `edu_group` remains in `cps_clean.csv.gz` for EDA. | 1 column |
| Encoding | Did not one-hot `region` (region dummies already exist). | Avoids a duplicated, perfectly collinear block. | 1 column |
| Encoding | One-hot encoded 7 nominal variables (race, marst, hispan, nativity, classwkr, educ99, adj_occ2name) with drop_first=True; binary dummies kept as-is. | Codes such as race=651 or educ99=15 are category labels without numeric meaning; one-hot avoids imposing a false order. drop_first removes the reference level (dummy-variable trap). | 77 -> 117 columns |
| Encoding | Dropped 21 linearly dependent dummy column(s): othrace, west, publicadmin, lehs, hrswork_missing, race_2, race_3, race_4, hispan_1.0, adj_occ2name_Business Operators, adj_occ2name_Community and Social Workers, adj_occ2name_Computer and Math Technicians, adj_occ2name_Consruction, Extraction, Installation, adj_occ2name_Farming, Fishing & Forestry, adj_occ2name_Lawyers, Judges,Physicans and dentists, adj_occ2name_Managers, adj_occ2name_Office and Admin Support, adj_occ2name_Production, adj_occ2name_Protective Service adj_occupations, adj_occ2name_Transportation and materials moving, adj_occ2name_financial Operators. | These columns are exact linear combinations of other columns and the intercept (exhaustive dummy sets); keeping them makes OLS ill-defined. | 21 columns |
| Scaling | StandardScaler on age, potexp, potexp2, wkswork1, uhrswork, year, numprec, hrswork, annhrs, wkswork2, inflate, union, perconexp — fitted on the 80 % training split only, applied to train and test. Dummies not scaled. | Put continuous features on a common scale for regularized/distance-based models; fitting on train only prevents test-set leakage. Tree models are unaffected, so the unscaled `cps_clean.csv.gz` is kept as well. | 13 columns |
| Train/test split | 80/20 split stratified by `female` (random_state=42): train 275,429 / test 68,858 rows. | Required so that scaling (and later model selection) is evaluated on unseen data; stratification keeps the sex ratio equal. |  |
